ukmt-sk-2022-03.title: Find the sector angles
ukmt-sk-2022-03.body:
The angles are $35,45,55,65,75,85,\dots$ and must total $360$: $35+45+55+65+75+85=360$, so there are six sectors. The smallest sector ($35^\circ$) is the seven people with one coin, so $5^\circ$ represents one person and the club has $360\div5=72$ people.

**Answer: 72**

ukmt-sk-2022-04.title: Equate areas
ukmt-sk-2022-04.body:
$S_1$ has area $x(4-y)$ and $S_2$ has area $y(9-x)$. Equal: $4x-xy=9y-xy$, so $4x=9y$ and $\frac xy=\frac94$. Then $\frac{360x}y=360\cdot\frac94=810$.

**Answer: 810**

ukmt-sk-2022-05.title: Worst case
ukmt-sk-2022-05.body:
The wall is at most $1925$ m$^2$ and a tin covers at least $17.5$ m$^2$. To be sure of covering the wall he needs $\frac{1925}{17.5}=110$ tins; to have at least half a tin spare he needs $110.5$, so he must buy $111$ tins.

**Answer: 111**

ukmt-sk-2022-06.title: Opposite faces
ukmt-sk-2022-06.body:
Two pyramids on opposite faces have heights adding to the side $s$, so their volumes add to $\frac13s^2\cdot s=\frac13s^3$, the same for each of the three pairs. Pairing: $200+1400=500+1100=1600$, so the sixth volume is $1600-1000=600$.

**Answer: 600**

ukmt-sk-2022-07.title: Factorise
ukmt-sk-2022-07.body:
$6075=3^5\cdot5^2$. So $1,3,5,15$ divide $N$; with six factors, $N=3^2\cdot5$ has factors $1,3,5,9,15,45$. Their product is $3^6\cdot5^3$, so the missing factor is $\frac{3^6\cdot5^3}{3^5\cdot5^2}=15$.

**Answer: 15**

ukmt-sk-2022-08.title: Incentre
ukmt-sk-2022-08.body:
$P$ is the incentre, so it is equidistant from all three sides: its distance to $AB$ and $AC$ is also $\sqrt{80000}$. Dropping perpendiculars to $AB$ and $AC$ gives a square with diagonal $AP$, so $AP=\sqrt{80000+80000}=\sqrt{160000}=400$.

**Answer: 400**

ukmt-sk-2022-09.title: Next occurrence
ukmt-sk-2022-09.body:
The next occurrence is $17{:}11{:}22$ on $17/11/22$, which is one day and one hour later: $25\times3600=90000$ seconds. So $\sqrt S=300$.

**Answer: 300**

ukmt-sk-2022-10.title: Vieta
ukmt-sk-2022-10.body:
For the first equation the sum of squares of roots is $a^2-2b$; for the second it is $b^2-2a$. Equal: $a^2-b^2=2b-2a$, i.e. $(a-b)(a+b)=-2(a-b)$. As $a\ne b$, $a+b=-2$. Then $500+10(-2)=480$.

**Answer: 480**

ukmt-sk-2022-11.title: Split into triangles
ukmt-sk-2022-11.body:
Let the circle have radius $r$. Joining the centre to the vertices splits the quadrilateral into four triangles with height $r$ on the sides, so area $=\frac12r\cdot\text{perimeter}$. The circle has area $\pi r^2=\frac12r\cdot(2\pi r)=\frac12r\cdot\text{circumference}$. Hence the area ratio equals the perimeter ratio, $4:3$, so $100\cdot4+49\cdot3=547$.

**Answer: 547**

ukmt-sk-2022-12.title: Express in one variable
ukmt-sk-2022-12.body:
Let $t=e^2$. Then $a=t-2$, $b=t+2$, $c=t/2$, $d=2t$. For $c$ to be an integer $t$ is even, so $e$ is even and $t\ge4$ (as $t=e^2$, $e\ge2$). Then $d=2t>t+2=b$, and $d$ exceeds $a$, $c$ and $e$ clearly ($e=\sqrt t<t$). So $d$ is largest and Gina has $104$ on the front.

**Answer: 104**

ukmt-sk-2022-14.title: Count pairs
ukmt-sk-2022-14.body:
There are $R$ red and $R+2$ green pupils. Pairs of different colour: $R(R+2)$. Red pairs: $\binom R2$. The condition $R(R+2)=3\binom R2=\frac{3R(R-1)}2$ gives $2(R+2)=3(R-1)$ (as $R>0$), so $R=7$. Then $343+49+7=399$.

**Answer: 399**

ukmt-sk-2022-15.title: 60-degree triangles
ukmt-sk-2022-15.body:
The square has side $10$. Its top-left vertex lies on the left side of the triangle, at height $10$, so the left base vertex is $\frac{10}{\tan60^\circ}=\frac{10}{\sqrt3}$ to the left of the square. The right base vertex coincides with the square's bottom-right corner, so the base is $10+\frac{10}{\sqrt3}$ and the perimeter is $30+\frac{30}{\sqrt3}=30+10\sqrt3$. So $a=30,b=10,p=3$ and $7a+5b+3p=210+50+9=269$.

**Answer: 269**

ukmt-sk-2022-16.title: Case analysis
ukmt-sk-2022-16.body:
If everyone were a Foe, all statements would be true, contradiction; so some Friend $A$ exists, and both neighbours of $A$ are Foes. A Foe must have at least one Friend neighbour. Label the circle $A,B,C,D,E,F,G$ with $B,G$ Foes. If $C$ is a Foe then $D$ is a Friend, $E$ a Foe, $F$ a Friend: Friends $A,D,F$. If $F$ is a Foe then $E$ is a Friend, $D$ a Foe, $C$ a Friend: Friends $A,C,E$. If $C$ and $F$ are both Friends then $D,E$ are Foes: Friends $A,C,F$. Always $3$ Friends.

**Answer: 3**

ukmt-sk-2022-16.title: Structure
ukmt-sk-2022-16.body:
Each Friend has two Foe neighbours, and each Foe has at least one Friend neighbour (otherwise it would be telling the truth). Let $f$ be the number of Friends. Counting Friend-Foe adjacencies: $2f$ in total, and each of the $7-f$ Foes accounts for $1$ or $2$ of them, so $7-f\le2f\le2(7-f)$, i.e. $\frac73\le f\le\frac{14}3$, so $f=3$ or $4$. If $f=4$ the Friends would need $8$ distinct adjacencies with $3$ Foes, but there are at most $6$. So $f=3$ (and it is possible, e.g. Friends at positions $1,3,5$ with Foes elsewhere... $A,C,F$ as above).

**Answer: 3**

ukmt-sk-2022-17.title: Search by q
ukmt-sk-2022-17.body:
$q=2$: $4k$ with $k$ odd product of two distinct odd primes: $100,108,116,124$ fail, $132=4\cdot3\cdot11$ works. $q=3$: multiples of $9$: $108=2^2\cdot3^3$ and $117=3^2\cdot13$ fail; $126=2\cdot3^2\cdot7$ works. $q=5$: $100,125$ fail and later values exceed $126$; $q\ge7$ gives at least $147$. So the smallest is $126$.

**Answer: 126**

ukmt-sk-2022-18.title: Cancel factorials
ukmt-sk-2022-18.body:
$\frac{20!}{11!}=12\cdot13\cdots20$ and $\frac{22!}{16!}=17\cdot18\cdots22$. Counting prime factors with multiplicity of $12,\dots,20$: $3,1,2,2,4,1,3,1,3$ gives $20$; of $17,\dots,22$: $1,3,1,3,2,2$ gives $12$. So $N=32$ and $N(N-2)=32\cdot30=960$.

**Answer: 960**

ukmt-sk-2022-19.title: Base 1, exponent 0, base -1
ukmt-sk-2022-19.body:
**Exponent $0$:** $x(x^2-1)(x^2-4)=0$ gives $x=-2,-1,0,1,2$; none makes the base $0$, so all $5$ work. **Base $1$:** $x^2-8x+14=0$ gives $x=4\pm\sqrt2$: $2$ solutions. **Base $-1$:** $x^2-8x+16=0$ gives $x=4$; the exponent there is $4^5-5\cdot4^3+16=720$, even, so $(-1)^{720}=1$ works. Total $5+2+1=8$.

**Answer: 8**

ukmt-sk-2022-20.title: Fill the grid
ukmt-sk-2022-20.body:
1 DOWN (two digits) is $16$ or $81$. If 3 ACROSS began with $6$, its largest proper factor would be at most $349$, violating the clue, so it begins with $1$ and 1 DOWN is $81$. Then 1 ACROSS is $81$ or $87$. If 2 DOWN began with $1$ it would be $125$ and 5 ACROSS $52$, making 4 DOWN end in $2$ (even); so 1 ACROSS is $87$, 2 DOWN is $729$ and 5 ACROSS is $91$. 4 DOWN ends in $1$ and is $21$, $51$ or $91$, giving 3 ACROSS $=122,125$ or $129$; only $125$ ($=100+25$, largest proper factor $25$) works, so 4 DOWN is $51$. The six answers are $87,125,91,81,729,51$ with sum $T=1164$, and the answer is $0.5T=582$.

**Answer: 582**
